newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ROMARIO'S REVIVAL CONTINUES WITH TWO MORE GOALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMARIO'S REVIVAL CONTINUES WITH TWO MORE GOALS.

text.p: The revival of Brazilian striker Romario continued at the weekend as he scored twice for Flamengo in their 5-0 away win over Barreira in the Rio de Janeiro championship.

Romario, who made his international comeback against Poland on Wednesday after a two-year absence from the national team, took his tally in the tournament to seven in five games, although all have come against modest opposition.
Brazil's 1994 World Cup hero has been determined to get his career back on the rails this year after seeing his fortunes take a nosedive with a series of problems on and off the field.

Vasco da Gama, who beat Fluminense 1-0, lead the first stage of the competition but have played two games more than Flamengo. The winners of each of the first three stages qualify for the final stage.
Corinthians went to the top of group two in the Sao Paulo championship by beating Uniao Sao Joao 1-0 away, even though they had two men sent off.

Striker Mirandinha was dismissed at halftime for a second bookable offence, his second red card in four games. Donizete, another forward, was sent off in the 83rd minute for kicking the ball into the net after he had been pulled up for offside. He had earlier been booked.
Striker Tulio, who joined the club in December from Botafogo, scored the winner, his fourth goal in six games.
Palmeiras and Guarani are level on points at the top of group one after beating Santos and Botafogo-Ribeirao Preto respectively. The top two teams in each group qualify for the play-offs.
